changelog: - **Amounts too small to show are no longer thrown away.** Until now the engine treated any amount at or under 0.000000001 as nothing: a connection that would move that little moved nothing, and a share that small out of a Gate was dropped with no record. Now every amount moves, however small, and the engine keeps an exact record of what each step moved. The canvas still shows a move only when it is above 0.000000001. When a step moves amounts too small to show, the run’s messages say how many, and the panel of a Pool they reached lists them with the Pool’s net change for the step. A node that moves such an amount counts as having fired, and an End that receives one ends the run. A connection with a rate at or under 0.000000001 is now a connection like any other: a Gate shares over it, a Converter needs it as an input, and where its target cannot take its share the Gate is held, as it would be by any other connection. A Pool’s capacity is tested with no tolerance, and a Pool is stored as the nearest number to its exact level, so stored values can differ from before in the last digit. In the bundled examples nothing is at or under 0.000000001; one shown digit changes at one checkpoint of the desalination example (1450101.91034538 L becomes 1450101.91034537 L). One thing is not settled: a node set to pull all that asks for 0.000000001 or less in all can run on a part of it. Stepping a model takes about twice as long as before (1.9 times on the bundled examples), and a Monte Carlo run of the recommended size about 1.3 times. A Monte Carlo result saved before this change is shown as stale until it is run again (engine revision 16).
